name: Hydrocephaly-Cerebellar Agenesis Syndrome

criteria.description: Complete or near-complete agenesis of the cerebellum confirmed by neuroimaging
Presence of communicating or non-communicating hydrocephalus detected by imaging
Clinical evidence of severe motor developmental delay or hypotonia
Exclusion of other major brain malformations or syndromic diagnoses

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of cerebellar agenesis and hydrocephalus with neurological dysfunction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on neuroimaging and clinical neurological assessment in neonates or infants.

laboratory: Routine labs typically normal; no specific biomarkers identified
imaging: MRI or CT showing complete or near-complete absence of cerebellar tissue
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases reported
other: Clinical neurological examination revealing hypotonia and developmental delay

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle
Partial cerebellar vermis hypoplasia rather than complete agenesis
Hypoplasia rather than agenesis of cerebellum
Genetic mutations identified in multiple subtypes

redFlags: Rapidly increasing head circumference in infancy
Severe motor developmental delay with hypotonia
Signs of increased intracranial pressure (vomiting, irritability, bulging fontanelle)
references: Barkovich AJ, et al. Pediatric Neuroimaging. 5th ed. 2012.
Volpe JJ. Neurology of the Newborn. 6th ed. 2018.
